title: Company-level OKRs: orbit map and tactical stretch mapping
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a company-level OKR "orbit map" that links top-level objectives to horizontally shared initiatives and identifies tactical "stretch" pieces each team should own for Q2 planning. This ticket covers the cross-functional mapping exercise, a dependency heatmap, and the handoff artifacts for engineering, design, and GTM partners.

Scope:
- Create an OKR-to-initiative fidelity matrix (CSV and Confluence doc) showing which initiatives materially move each company objective.
- Build a dependency heatmap that surfaces critical path work and single-team single-point-of-failure initiatives.
- Define tactical stretch items for each initiative (2–3 per team) with owner, estimate, and success metric.
- Produce a rollout runway and escalation path for deconfliction across Product, Eng, Design, Research, and Sales.
- Deliver an artifacts bundle: Confluence PRD, shared Drive folder with CSVs, a Notion/Confluence one-pager for exec review, and a short Loom walkthrough.

Success metrics:
- Exec sign-off on the orbit map and tactical stretch list by March 21.
- 90% of initiative owners acknowledge their defacto dependencies and owners in the spreadsheet within 48 hours of share.
- A dependency list with mitigation plans for all 'high' impact items (as labeled in the heatmap).

Why now: Our current planning cycle shows ambiguous ownership between Dedicated and Serving teams for three cross-cutting initiatives; this increases risk of missed SLOs and duplicate work. The orbit map is intended to reduce ambiguity and speed up execution during Q2 planning and capacity commits.

acceptance_criteria: Exec one-pager and orbit map accepted in leadership sync (recorded approval in Confluence).
All initiatives in the matrix have an owner, a primary dependency list, and at least one tactical stretch item assigned.
Dependency heatmap graded and all 'high' impact items have an agreed mitigation or escalation owner.
Artifacts uploaded to shared Drive and linked in the Confluence one-pager; Loom walkthrough recorded and shared.
